jobs.title: Director, AI Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Director, Enterprise AI Platform Engineering

Job Description

BMO is building a dedicated AI Engineering function to deliver the platform capabilities that make enterprise AI safe, governed, and scalable across our business domains and regulatory regimes. We are seeking an experienced technical leader to own the core infrastructure that governs and enforces how AI runs at BMO
- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

This is a build-and-run
leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Required Core Skills

Organizational & People Leadership

8+ years in technical platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML engineering roles in a large enterprise, including 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams.
Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated team building across blended teams — integrating net-new hires with reallocated and seconded internal engineers into a single high-performing team with shared identity and standards.
Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Demonstrated experience building and operating platform capabilities at scale — API gateways, policy/authorization systems, identity/workload-identity infrastructure, observability pipelines, or equivalent shared services.
Strong knowledge of GenAI platform engineering: LLM/AI gateways, model routing and abstraction, RAG and agentic patterns, guardrails, and AI evaluation approaches.
Hands-on experience with policy-as-code and authorization systems (Cedar, OPA/Rego, or equivalent) and GitOps-based distribution.
Experience with workload identity and zero-trust patterns (SPIFFE/SPIRE, mTLS, token exchange, federated identity) — or strong adjacent identity/security engineering depth.
Strong observability engineering background: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and telemetry pipelines across operational, security, and compliance domains.
Multi-cloud fluency (AWS and Azure preferred), cloud-native architecture, containerization/Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI/ML tooling (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, LangChain, or equivalents) sufficient to lead technical direction.
Proven CI/CD, DevSecOps, and MLOps/LLMOps delivery experience.

Governance, Strategy & Communication

Solid grounding in Responsible AI, AI/data governance, privacy, and — ideally — model-risk management and financial-services regulatory expectations.
Executive-grade communication and relationship management across technical and senior-leadership audiences (written, verbal, and presentation).
Strategic and organizational management skills, including multi-year roadmap planning, budgeting, forecasting, and vendor engagement in partnership with Vendor Management.
A critical thinker with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization abilities across a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio.

Education & Certifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline (Master's preferred).
Relevant certifications an asset: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) architecture or ML/AI certifications, Kubernetes (CKA/CKAD), security/identity certifications, or enterprise architecture (TOGAF or equivalent).

Salary:

$120,000.00 - $215,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type.

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role, and may include a commission structure. Salaries for part-time roles will be pro-rated based on number of hours regularly worked. For commission roles, the salary listed above represents BMO Financial Group’s expected target for the first year in this position.

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. BMO also offers health insurance, tuition reimbursement, accident and life insurance, and retirement savings plans. To view more details of our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.bmo.com/global/en/Total-Rewards

About Us

At BMO we are driven by a shared Purpose: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life. It calls on us to create lasting, positive change for our customers, our communities and our people. By working together, innovating and pushing boundaries, we transform lives and businesses, and power economic growth around the world.

As a member of the BMO team you are valued, respected and heard, and you have more ways to grow and make an impact. We strive to help you make an impact from day one – for yourself and our customers. We’ll support you with the tools and resources you need to reach new milestones, as you help our customers reach theirs. From in-depth training and coaching, to manager support and network-building opportunities, we’ll help you gain valuable experience, and broaden your skillset.

To find out more visit us at https://jobs.bmo.com/ca/en

BMO is committed to an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace. By learning from each other’s differences, we gain strength through our people and our perspectives. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. To request accommodation, please contact your recruiter.

Note to Recruiters: BMO does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to BMO, directly or indirectly, will be considered BMO property. BMO will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. jobs.title: 1835 - Senior Director - Global Delivery Lead - Data Retention
jobs.description:
Please send your resume at anila.dada@amyantek.com if you are interested in this 13 month contract with Sunlife with a possibility of extension, If you are not interested, please feel free to pass it in your network for anyone looking for work.

Position title:
1835 - Senior Director - Global Delivery Lead - Data Retention
Working Status:
Hybrid - Limited onsite presence required, typically one to two days per month (less than one day per week on average).
Location:
227 King Street South, Waterloo, ON N2J 4C5 or 1 York Street, Toronto, ON
Background Check:
Tier 1 checks
Start Date:
November 04, 2026
End Date:
December 15, 2027
Work Hours:
Standard business hours, Monday to Friday, either 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. or 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Flexibility is required on occasion to accommodate meetings with global stakeholders, including occasional early morning or evening calls with Asia-based partners.

Manager Notes:

Critical Industry Experience

Strong Preference

Financial Services experience is viewed as a requirement rather than a nice-to-have.
Candidates need credibility in regulated environments and should understand:
Regulatory-driven transformation programs.
Enterprise risk remediation.
Governance and control programs.

Highly Desired

Candidates who have worked on:
OSFI-driven initiatives.
E-21 related programs.
E-23 related programs.
Regulatory compliance and remediation efforts within financial institutions.

Proven Enterprise Program Leader

The hiring manager emphasized that the ideal candidate has repeatedly led large-scale, complex enterprise programs and successfully navigated ambiguity and organizational complexity.
Candidates should demonstrate:
Multiple examples of leading enterprise-wide programs.
Ownership of a portfolio or program of projects versus a single project.
A track record of turning difficult, complex situations into successful outcomes.
Experience building PMOs and governance models from scratch.

Exceptional Stakeholder Management

This is one of the most important success factors.
The individual will often be responsible for influencing business units and executives to take action, even when they do not directly report to them.
Strong candidates will have:
Executive presence.
Experience influencing AVPs, VPs, SVPs, and CIO-level leaders.
Strong relationship-building skills.
Ability to push for accountability while maintaining positive partnerships.

Data Governance / Data Retention Expertise

While Sally stated she may consider a truly exceptional program leader without direct data retention experience, candidates with data governance and data retention backgrounds will have a significant advantage because they will gain credibility much faster.
Preferred experience includes:
Data Governance
Data Retention
Records & Information Management
Regulatory remediation
Data lifecycle management
Information security-related data programs

Critical Skills / Must-Haves:

10+ years of progressive experience leading large, complex enterprise programs, including global or multi-business transformation.
Demonstrated success building and running a large program office with multiple project managers, workstreams, delivery partners and senior sponsors.
Strong command of program governance, integrated planning, dependency management, RAID management, financial oversight, resource planning and executive reporting.
Experience delivering programs in data governance, data management, records and information management, cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory remediation, technology risk or related domains.
Ability to translate strategy and risk objectives into practical work packages, milestones, measures and accountable execution.
Experience leading federated programs where central standards and governance support execution by business or regional teams.
Working knowledge of structured and unstructured data environments, data lifecycle practices, classification, retention and disposition concepts.
Experience managing consulting firms, systems integrators and specialist vendors in outcome-based engagements.

Nice-to-Haves:

Financial services, insurance or another highly regulated industry.
Enterprise data governance, data lifecycle management, information management or data remediation.
Cyber risk reduction, privacy, audit, regulatory remediation or control transformation.
Operating-model design, organizational change and business adoption.
Agile and traditional delivery methods, with sound judgment on where each approach fits.

Education:
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Program management certification is an asset.

Ideal Candidate Profile

A senior program leader who can demonstrate:
10+ years leading large enterprise programs
Financial Services experience
Data Governance / Data Retention experience
Regulatory remediation experience
OSFI E-21 or E-23 exposure
Experience building PMOs and governance structures from scratch
Strong executive communication skills
Ability to influence senior stakeholders without direct authority
Global program delivery experience
Proven track record delivering multiple complex transformation programs successfully over time

Experience working across:

Multiple geographies
Large distributed stakeholder groups
Global governance models

Flexibility for occasional early morning or evening meetings with Asia-based stakeholders is expected

The opportunity

We are seeking a senior global delivery leader to establish and lead the program office for the Global Data Retention Management Program. The program will coordinate enterprise efforts to identify, secure, classify and remediate over-retained structured and unstructured data, using a risk-based approach and a common global framework. The role is accountable for turning a complex cross-enterprise mandate into an executable roadmap, strong governance, transparent reporting and measurable outcomes.
This is a hands-on leadership role for a self-starter who creates clarity, builds momentum and takes ownership. The successful candidate will work across business groups and control functions, lead a team of project managers and workstream leads, and engage senior business and technology leaders to resolve issues and maintain alignment.

Key accountabilities

Own integrated delivery across discovery, planning, execution and transition to sustainable business-as-usual controls.
Establish and run the program management office, including the integrated roadmap, and master schedule. Coordinate with regional delivery teams on their work breakdown structure, resource plan, financial controls and delivery standards.
Design and operate program governance, including steering committee, governance committee and working-team forums, with clear decision rights, escalation paths and accountabilities.
Lead multiple project managers, workstream leads, internal teams and external delivery partners. Set expectations, remove barriers and drive timely decisions.
Develop executive communication and reporting models covering progress, outcomes, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, financials and capacity.
Create and maintain stakeholder, governance, communications, change and adoption plans suited to a global, federated delivery model.
Partner with business groups to sequence work based on risk, readiness, dependencies and capacity while avoiding duplication with related initiatives.
Drive consistent execution across data inventory, risk tiering, security controls, classification, retention, disposition and sustainment workstreams.
Ensure delivery evidence, controls and reporting are clear, traceable and suitable for senior management, audit and regulatory review.
Manage vendors and systems integrators, including scope, deliverables, commercial performance, quality and knowledge transfer.

Measures of success

A credible global roadmap, governance model and integrated delivery plan are established and actively used.
Senior leaders have clear, concise and timely visibility into outcomes, trade-offs, risks and decisions.
Workstreams have accountable owners, realistic plans and disciplined execution rhythms.
Priority data risks are addressed through a repeatable model that business groups can sustain.

Experience and expertise

Stakeholder leadership

Operate confidently with Business Group CIOs and senior business leaders at VP and SVP levels.
Build alignment across Technology, Data, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Risk, Privacy, Compliance, Legal, Records Management, Audit and business teams.
Frame complex issues simply, present clear options and secure timely decisions without overloading leaders with detail.
Influence across organizational boundaries, manage competing priorities and maintain constructive challenge when commitments are at risk.
Create trusted relationships while preserving clear accountability for outcomes, decisions and follow-through.

Leadership competencies

Ownership and drive
Acts as the accountable leader, anticipates needs and follows issues through to resolution.
Self-directed execution
Creates structure from ambiguity, mobilizes quickly and works effectively with limited direction.
Enterprise perspective
Connects delivery choices to risk reduction, business outcomes and long-term sustainability.
Executive communication
Communicates with precision, adapts to the audience and makes decisions easy to understand.
People leadership
Sets high standards, develops team members and creates a culture of accountability and collaboration. (No direct people management)
Pragmatic judgment
Balances pace, control, cost, capacity and quality to keep a complex program moving.

Why this role matters

The Global Data Retention Management Program addresses a material enterprise need: reducing cyber, privacy and regulatory risk while creating stronger and more sustainable control over data assets (structured and unstructured). This role will shape how the organization mobilizes, governs and executes a complex global transformation, while building a delivery model that can be sustained across business groups.

Top Priorities (First 6-12 Months)

First 3 Months

Shape and define the overall Global Data Retention Program.
Build the program roadmap and execution plan.
Identify required workstreams and establish the PMO structure.
Develop governance, reporting, stakeholder engagement, and delivery plans.

Months 4+

Drive execution and oversight of all workstreams.
Coordinate delivery across multiple business groups.
Influence stakeholders to complete required remediation activities.
Maintain executive visibility and program momentum.

jobs.title: Director, Insights, Innovation and RandD (18-month contract)
jobs.description:
The Director, Insights, Innovation, & R&D leads the consumer insight, menu innovation, product development, and food quality agenda for KFC Canada. This role turns consumer and business insight into a growth-driving innovation pipeline, modernizes KFC's core products, and leads the FIT (Food Innovation & Technology aka Product Development) team from concept through commercialization. The Director partners closely with Marketing, Operations, Supply Chain and franchisees to ensure products are distinctive, consumer-led, operationally executable and delivered to KFC quality and food safety standards. If you are a leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, can navigate ambiguity with action, has ambition to deliver impact and a spirit of what is possible – KFC is an environment that will empower and support your success.

Own the integrated consumer insights, menu strategy and innovation agenda, translating consumer, category and cultural insight into clear growth opportunities and the short-, medium- and long-term pipeline and business.
Lead the FIT team and end-to-end product development process, from culinary/product brief and prototyping through consumer validation, restaurant testing, commercialization and launch.
Modernize and continuously improve KFC Canada's core food portfolio, protecting what consumers love while improving taste, quality, consistency, value and relevance.
Build and deliver a differentiated innovation pipeline that supports the Marketing growth calendar, creates newsworthy reasons to choose KFC and strengthens the brand across priority occasions and consumer groups.
Act as guardian of KFC Canada's food philosophy and architect of the menu vision, defining the principles, product standards and strategic choices that guide product development and renovation.
Lead consumer insights across internal resources and agency partners, ensuring customer understanding is embedded in brand strategy, calendar development, innovation, value and broader business planning.
Set clear innovation learning agendas and stage gates; use consumer, operational and commercial evidence to make fast decisions on what to advance, optimize or stop.
Partner with Brand, Retail Marketing, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance and franchisees to ensure innovation is commercially compelling, operationally executable, scalable and supported by strong launch plans.
Own R&D prioritization, resources and ways of working, ensuring the team balances core product improvement, calendar innovation, longer-term pipeline development and rapid test-and-learn opportunities.
Provide leadership oversight of Quality Assurance within the team remit, ensuring robust product and supplier standards, food safety and quality systems, issue escalation, and continuous improvement in partnership with Operations and Supply Chain.
Deliver credible thought leadership and compelling recommendations to KFC Canada LT, franchisees and cross-functional stakeholders, aligning the system behind bold but evidence-based growth choices.
Build a high-performing, connected Insights, Innovation, R&D and QA capability with clear accountability, strong talent development and effective collaboration across the broader business.

Education/Certifications

Required: Post-secondary degree in business, marketing, or related discipline
Preferred: MBA

Experience

10+ years of progressive experience across consumer insights, innovation, product development/R&D, brand, food science or related commercial functions
Demonstrated experience leading teams and an end-to-end food innovation pipeline from insight and concept through product development, testing, commercialization and launch
Style that inspires and unites cross-functional teams, bringing clarity in strategy and empowering whilst holding accountable with a spirit of taking people with you.
Compelling communications capability, translating complex ideas simply to bring clarity and alignment across a diverse set of stakeholders.
Strong track record of translating consumer insight into commercial growth strategies and high-impact innovation.
Strong understanding of operations, supply chain and commercialization requirements; able to balance consumer desirability, operational feasibility and commercial viability.
Proven ability to modernize core products while building a forward-looking innovation pipeline.
Ability to influence senior leaders, franchisees, and complex matrixed stakeholders through ambiguity and transformation.
Ability to effectively develop and lead high-performing technical and commercial talent.
Ability to balance enterprise-level strategic thinking with curiosity, creativity, pace, and hands-on problem solving.
A passion for food, consumers, and emerging trends

We’d prefer this role to have…

Prior experience in QSR, food manufacturing/FMCG, or food retail

What makes KFC a great place to work?

Our People.
We invest in people capability above all else, with a proven track record of developing internal talent to leadership levels across the business both in Canada and globally. We hire and develop people who lead with Smart, Heart and Courage to make a big impact on the business today and grow into leaders of the future.

Our Culture.
We are known for a culture that rewards and recognizes bold results and promises everyone a seat at our table. We focus on your personal development as much as your professional development to ensure you can bring your best self to work.

Why you’ll love working here

Hybrid work model (2-3 days per week in office)
Paid vacation and personal days, plus 10 paid KFC Canada holidays in addition to statutory holidays.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits, including HSA and PSA options that allow you to personalize your coverage, plus life insurance and disability coverage, with employer-paid premiums
Family-inclusive Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and virtual care
Paid parental leave with salary top-up
RRSP and DPSP retirement programs with employer matching
Annual tuition reimbursement program
Employee referral rewards
And so much more!

Note: remuneration, benefits, and other perks may vary by role, employment status, eligibility, and other relevant factors.

Additional Information

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

We thank all applicants for their interest in joining KFC Canada; however, only those selected for further screening will be contacted. Applicants are assessed based on skills and experience relevant to the role. Canadian experience is not required.

KFC Canada is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace where everyone feels they belong. In accordance with applicable laws, we are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to meet the needs of applicants. If you require accommodation at any stage of the hiring process, please let us know.

The expected hiring range for this role is $160,000 to $210,000 CAD , inclusive of base salary. Final compensation will be based on factors such as skills, experience, qualifications, and internal equity.

KFC Canada uses artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools to support certain aspects of the recruitment process, including application screening and assessment, in accordance with applicable legislation. All final hiring decisions are made by human decision-makers.
